record.notes: Cover dated October 2024; comments were invited until 29 November 2024. It describes itself as a step towards a National AI Policy that would be the basis for AI regulations and potentially an AI Act. The Draft South Africa National AI Policy gazetted on 10 April 2026 (ZA-01), which calls this document the framework of August 2024, was based on it and on the 32 submissions received on it; that draft was later withdrawn.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the OECD.AI policy-initiative page (12 and 18 Oct 2026; only the site menu differs between the two copies) and the OECD-hosted PDF of the framework (12 Oct 2026, 20 pages). The PDF confirms the title, the department, the October 2024 date, the comment deadline of 29 November 2024 and the twelve pillars; the OECD.AI page confirms publication in October 2024 by the department. No copy on a South African government site is stored, so the record rests on another official body's copy. The earlier notes cited law-firm and press accounts of an August 2024 circulation and of release dates in October 2024; these are not stored and are no longer cited, and the gazetted draft policy of April 2026 (ZA-01, stored for that record) itself calls this the framework of August 2024. A department statement that a revised draft would go to Cabinet by November 2026, also in the earlier notes, is not among the stored files and is no longer cited. Nothing stored shows the framework withdrawn.

judgment.status_reasoning: A discussion framework published by the department for comment until 29 November 2024, as a step towards a National AI Policy. The draft policy built on it (ZA-01) was gazetted in April 2026 and then withdrawn, so nothing has replaced the framework, and nothing stored shows the framework itself withdrawn. OECD.AI's 'Proposed or under development' describes the policy process, not this published document. Published (non-binding, current), legal force Non-binding, as before.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A national AI policy framework whose pillars include ethical AI guidelines, safety and security with AI risk management, transparency and explainability, fairness, human control of critical AI decisions and a code of conduct; its governance content is its main content, so no scope_note.
judgment.date_reasoning: The cover reads 'October 2024' and OECD.AI says 'published in October 2024'; the gazetted draft policy of April 2026 calls it the framework of August 2024. The document's own date is kept (2024-10) and the August 2024 dating goes in the notes.
judgment.topics_reasoning: Unchanged and supported: human oversight (6.10 human-in-the-loop for critical AI decisions), transparency & labelling (6.8 transparency and explainability), accountability & liability (6.8 accountability through explainability, 6.11 code of conduct), public-sector use (6.4 guidelines for AI in government operations). The summary is unchanged; its pillar claims are quoted above.

open_questions: No copy of the framework on a South African government site is among the stored files; the record rests on the OECD-hosted copy.
Whether the department has published or announced a revised draft national AI policy after the withdrawal of ZA-01 in June 2026 is not shown by any stored file.
